The base adapter hook resolve_execution_engine exists with the default behavior described, and a unit test shows an adapter without declared engines returns a platform_default receipt for `default` and raises for anything else

polars-df declares its engines in the manifest exactly as the ADR specifies; the SQL `polars` platform declares none; make platform-manifest-check passes and registry/inventory counts are unchanged apart from the new capability

tests/unit/core/test_execution_vocabulary_parity.py passes on the current tree with the ADR's grandfather list, fails when a test fixture registers a new bare-word canonical key such as `engine` on another platform (demonstrated in the PR), and runs in the make pr-preflight fast lane
No CLI, MCP, adapter or result-bundle behavior changes in this PR: existing unit tests pass unchanged and a polars-df tpch SF 0.01 dry run produces the same output as before
Production diff is at most about 250 lines excluding tests, or the split was agreed with the user
PR merged through the normal flow; durable text carries no tracker IDs

description:
Establish the platform-neutral framework from the accepted ADR without changing any user-facing behavior yet.

Work:
1. New benchbox/core/execution_engine.py: the closed class vocabulary, the `default` sentinel, an ExecutionEngineReceipt dataclass (requested, applied, applied_class, applied_native, resolution, observed, observed_source), supported_execution_engines(platform) read from the platform registry, resolve_requested(platform, value) that fails closed with an error listing the allowed names, and ExecutionEngineUnavailableError.
2. Adapter contract: a hook resolve_execution_engine(requested) -> ExecutionEngineReceipt on the base platform adapter (SQL and DataFrame bases), whose default accepts only `default` and returns a receipt with resolution=platform_default and observed=not_captured. Every later engine declaration implements this one hook.
3. Manifest capability `execution_engines` (per ADR D3): validate in core/platform_manifest.py (_validate_capabilities, near :100-130): unknown class, a platform declaring `default`, duplicate names, missing fields, and selectable flag type are rejected. Parse into an ExecutionEngineCapability on PlatformCapability (core/platform_registry.py:97-106, 528-572) with accessors mirroring supports_deployment_mode.
4. Declare polars-df engines per the ADR (expected: auto=adaptive, in-memory, streaming). `gpu` is not declared; adding it later needs its own item with a cudf-polars dependency gate. The SQL-mode `polars` platform declares none.
5. Parity test tests/unit/core/test_execution_vocabulary_parity.py: every manifest class is in the core list; one value name maps to one class across all platforms; no platform registers a reserved bare-word canonical key (ADR D11, with aliases treated per D12) outside the grandfather list, checked across PlatformHookRegistry specs, cli/platform_defaults.py and the MCP allowlist; anonymizer identifier_keys contain none of the core vocabulary keys. Add the test to the fast lane run by make pr-preflight.
6. Regenerate generated inventories with make platform-manifest (never by hand).
